$comment: HISTORICAL PILOT EVIDENCE. Labeled, non-authoritative, maintainer-unreviewed. Not a benchmark, forecast, service level, or promise that a run will find a bug.
label: historical-pilot-evidence
disclaimer: This record exists so adopters can see the prior evidence behind the Bug Bash design instead of an unsourced claim.
It describes one historical pilot run by maintainers before this campaign existed. The shipped harness did not produce it and has not reproduced it.
No maintainer confirmed either candidate as a defect. Treat both as unreviewed hypotheses, not as known bugs in the named projects.
Counts below describe that single pilot only. They are not an expected yield, a success rate, or a commitment that any run surfaces a finding.
The expected outcome of a first Bug Bash run is no-finding.

excluded.reason: Fixtures must never seed live source, reproductions, or repairs into a new investigation.

scope.selectionBasis: existing tests already present in the pinned revisions

repositories.note: Identified in the pilot only by project name; no repository identifier or revision was carried into this record.
Third pinned repository counted in the pilot; no identifier was carried into this record.

candidates.summary: Impossible calendar dates were accepted where a validated date was expected.
candidates.contractClaimed: A date-shaped value that cannot exist on the calendar should be rejected rather than normalized or stored.

candidates.summary: Chunking an empty input produced a result that disagreed with the documented boundary behavior.
candidates.contractClaimed: A chunking helper given empty input should return the documented empty-input result rather than a differently shaped value.

designLessons: A failing test is not a bug: both candidates needed a stated contract before a failure meant anything.
A reproduction must be replayed on the original pinned revision in a fresh environment before it is believable.
Setup and environment failures dominated early noise and must be classified separately from product behavior.
Passing tests after a patch are not evidence that the repair is correct; boundaries must be challenged and weakened tests detected.
Unbounded search starves verification, so verification budget is reserved up front.
